text:
four days in, and the conversations got bigger than the conference itself. 🇮🇳

a little late, but @EFDevcon final day in mumbai deserved a proper recap.

from @ETHGlobal Pragma to technical discussions and conversations with brilliant leaders and creative minds, here’s what stood out.

> ETHGlobal Pragma Mumbai

a different conference experience. one track, curated talks and focused conversations. less running between stages, more time understanding what people are building and why.

> the open source network state

Balaji S. Srinivasan’s talk at @ETHIndiaco explored a bigger question: what happens when communities can build institutions and coordinate globally through open technology? this conversation goes far beyond crypto.

> privacy beyond the buzzword

HOPR’s private transport, peer payments and Gnosis VPN workshop raised an important question: how do we communicate without exposing unnecessary metadata?

> the infrastructure underneath decentralisation

privacy isn’t just about transactions. protecting network communication, reducing metadata leakage and resisting censorship are fundamental to keeping permissionless systems open.

> the people shaping the ecosystem

met incredible leaders, builders and creative minds. some of the best conversations happened away from the stage, without slides or agendas.

> beyond the protocol

AI, finance, identity, privacy and open infrastructure are becoming increasingly connected. the boundaries are blurring, and that’s where some interesting opportunities are emerging.

> the creative layer

this industry needs more people thinking deeply about product experience, brand, storytelling and culture. technology moves quickly, but communicating its value matters just as much.

> a little perspective

don’t let conference criticism, hot takes and noise distract you from your own work. focus on building, learning and contributing. some people might need a little Burnol to get over their conference experience. 😂

> and the merch hunters?

they’re everywhere. don’t confuse a few people chasing free merch with the actual builders and potential of an entire ecosystem.

one thought to close the week:

be kind. give people credit. share knowledge, make introductions and celebrate good work.

culture isn’t built through conference stages or social media commentary. it’s built through how we treat people and contribute to the ecosystem.

ethereum’s biggest opportunity isn’t just what its technology can do today. it’s what it enables people to build, own, coordinate and organise tomorrow.

that’s the bigger story.

i explore these intersections through The Protocol, my research and writing project on crypto, product, design, culture and the future of the internet.

designprotocol (dot) substack (dot) com

and a special thank you to the organisers, volunteers, support staff and the entire Ethereum team. so much work happens behind the scenes. genuinely appreciate everyone who made this experience possible. ❤️

bringing @EFDevcon to India was one of the best decisions. the energy, hospitality and people made this a wonderful experience.

mumbai, you delivered. 🇮🇳
see you at devcon lisbon. 🇵🇹🦄

On Fragmentation for Tokenized Equities:
I’d say tokenization doesn’t fix composability, and TradFi has the same problem: every broker holding is its own wrapper. The difference is TradFi has DTC underneath, so you can move between brokers 1:1 because they all point to the same share.

Tokenized stocks don’t have that layer yet. The closest fix is a unified DEX pool across issuers, something like Curve’s 3pool for DAI-USDC-USDT.
author: tomwanhh
quoted_text:
Tokenized equities are where stablecoins were in their early days.

The core problem: most tokenized stocks today are issued by companies that also run the exchange and the layer one. Each of these players has zero incentive to list or trade a competitor’s standard.

The result is ten competing standards and fragmented liquidity.

What the market needs is a neutral issuer, one that doesn’t own every layer of the stack.

The story keeps getting crazier. To recap everything that has been reported so far: 

- The US intelligence community discovered that Jensen Huang, the CEO of the largest company in the world, was sleeping with Alice Huang, a Chinese spy and an executive at Megaspeed. (FT)
- Multiple independent investigations have concluded that Megaspeed is likely a Chinese cutout, which helps Chinese companies access AI chips or circumvent export controls. (NYT and Bloomberg) 
- The US intelligence community also concluded that Alice Huang’s goal was to convince Jensen to lobby the U.S. government to loosen export controls on advanced AI chips. (NYT)
- The intelligence community relayed this information to “a small group of top US government officials” earlier this year. (FT)
- Over the last year, Jensen Huang has repeatedly lobbied the U.S. government to loosen export controls on advanced chips. @BISgov has done so, not only by permitting the export of H200 chips to China, but also not enforcing export controls that would have required a license for exports of the most advanced Blackwell chips to Megaspeed and Southeast Asia.
- Although @CommerceGov leadership was presumably briefed on this information by the U.S. intelligence community, @BISgov has taken no actions to tighten controls on Megaspeed or Southeast Asia. 
- Megaspeed remains a preferred cloud partner of Nvidia, and continues to receive Nvidia Blackwell chips despite employing a Chinese spy who reportedly is romantically engaged with the CEO of Nvidia. 
- Tens of billions of dollars worth of AI chips have been exported to Southeast Asia this year alone, and Malaysia and Singapore are now two of the four largest importers of AI chips in the world. 

What is going on here??? We need answers. The question of who gets the most advanced AI chips in the world is literally the defining strategic question of our time. And not only does it seem like the MSS may be directly influencing the debate on export controls in the United States, but also @CommerceGov is refusing to listen to the warnings of the IC on this issue. This is beyond strange at this point. 

The fallout from this story will be massive. Obviously, the motivations underpinning Nvidia’s policy views opposing export controls must now all be questioned. But also, how did @BISgov sit on this information and has still taken no actions? We need answers.

text:
团队同时使用 Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode 开发，最头疼的问题之一是代码出了 Bug，却不知道是哪一个 Agent 改的，更不知道它当时收到了什么 Prompt、调用了哪些工具。

Git 能记录代码改了什么，却很难解释 AI 为什么这么改。

最近发现一个开源项目 Atlas，专门解决这个问题。

它会记录 Coding Agent 的完整会话，包括 Prompt、回复、工具调用、文件修改和代码补丁，再将这些记录与 Git Commit 关联起来。

这样排查问题时，不仅能看到某次提交的 Diff，还能追溯是哪一个 Agent、在哪次会话中、根据什么上下文完成了修改。

即使代码经过 amend 或 rebase，Atlas 也会尝试保留对应关系。

它还支持多个 Agent 并行工作、共享项目记忆，以及团队成员查看和讨论彼此的 Agent 会话。

会话记录可以保存在本地，团队协作时再按需同步。不过，记录执行历史不等于能够完整复现每一次 AI 推理。

Git 解决的是代码版本管理，Atlas 想补上的是 AI 开发过程中的上下文追溯。

当多个 Coding Agent 开始参与同一个项目，知道代码改了什么已经不够了，还得知道它为什么这么改。

这波感觉Binance没啥问题，但是这个回复感觉越抹越黑了，我大概看懂了，冒昧中译中一下。

Binance Global用户有一套UID.A，Binance TH用户有一套UID.B，两个站完全就是独立站（不能通过UID转账），两边就是存在用户UID一样的情况，就像你的QQ号和Binance UID也有可能一样。

这个用户从Binance Global想转账到Binance TH的账户，因为不知道两个站点是独立站，所以用了UID转账（但其实不互通的），输入了Binance TH的UID，但是这个UID在Binance Global是对应另一个用户的账户。转账的时候其实会弹出二次确认，要用户检验收款账户的用户名是否一致，这一步其实是能发现问题的。

Binance作为金融机构在没有授权的情况下不能直接转走已经收到资金的用户资产，只能冻结后帮转错的用户联系Global这边的用户确认退回，或者等待执法机构介入配合。

quoted_text:
每个人在币安都只会有一个UID，且是独立的，并不存在撞号。我理解你的感受，从联系我开始到现在，全程我和4个员工跟踪了前因后果。
我简单描述一下背景：您把币安的钱转到币安（泰国），正常这属于跨站转账，需要用地址或者二维码，但你在转账过程中在币安直接输入UID转账，虽然我们有二次确认环节，但你没有仔细看。你发现转错后，直接找了我。我本人和4个人的团队一直在协助，第一时间帮忙冻结了这笔钱，但因为这个收到钱的持仓用户并不活跃，我们也在反复联系对方，但对方没有响应。我们做了应该做的，甚至设身处地考虑你打错了钱会着急，所以尽可能帮忙。
对方并不是犯罪，是您打错币，如果对方坚持不退只能我们客服介入谈判。你着急，我们建议让你通过报警执法介入，我们再协助沟通。但你在泰国报警，您在您希望收款的泰国报警要求币安主站把另外一个国家的币安用户的资产直接划拨给你，这不符合执法流程，报警应该在你希望找的用户国家所在地而不是泰国。
之前处理过很多打错币的情况，大额打错几千万美金，也是我们及时拦住帮忙追的，而且当时用户坚持不退，也是我们协助谈判，最后到双方能接受的范围和解。
我理解你的难处，团队也一直在跟踪进展，得到的就是这篇长文，我们会继续联系另外一个用户协商，但你打错币这事儿，在泰国报警确实帮不上忙，那是你的钱想去没去成的目的地。
最后提醒大家，币安土耳其，币安泰国，币安美国等本地法币交易平台是独立平台，并不共享账号系统，日常转账提币时请仔细检查地址和UID。

quoted_text:
民主党这招停建算力中新其实就是权利洗牌，利益再分配，但不只是两党，还有居民和大企业之间的博弈。

以德州为例，Hinojosa的官方主张是暂停新增项目，直到州议会建立居民保护措施，并重新处理税收优惠，并没有提出永久关闭所有数据中心。

而且早在 9 月 21 日 共和党州长 Abbott就实际下令暂停相关许可，等待审计，并要求项目承担电力基础设施成本。

所以这次变化其实是借着中期选举把原来民众对政府牺牲底层利益挤占资源补贴企业扩张的势头叫停了，未来会让数据中心自己掏更多钱去升级电网，掏钱买更贵的水，交更多的税。

这样原来靠发行企业债扩张的算力中心的运营成本就进一步上升，加上融资成本本就不低，及终端收入始终无法覆盖成本，才导致了对资金链断裂预期下的股价恐慌式崩盘。

而且即使算力中心建设是暂时性叫停也会有巨大的影响，长鑫追赶很快：第六代平台完成工程样片验证，预计年底将首代 4F² DDR5 RDIMM 产品送样、HBM3E已经小批量投产。关键追赶期下美方的叫停无疑是给竞争对手一个绝佳的赶超时机，进一步压缩了美韩系存储未来的盈利预期。

那么综合来看，对于闪迪持仓我大概会等情绪性的超跌反弹之后再走，这样可以少亏甚至不亏，但在两党博弈接近达成之前，可能不适合长线持仓了。

Using agentic AI at work becomes as standard as using a computer.

3. Tiny teams build giant companies

1-5 person empires become a real path for great entrepreneurs. No need for bloated teams.

4. Intelligence becomes nearly free

Inference costs are down ~99% in three years. Most AI becomes free and accessible by 2028 at the latest.

5. AI starts making real scientific breakthroughs

Expect major progress in areas like cancer treatment and vaccines.

6. The most powerful models get gatekept

The public will no longer have access to the best models

7. The AI-native gap becomes the new wealth gap

AI-skilled workers already earn +62% more (PwC). I think that gap only compounds from here.

Insane times we're living through.

text:
最近创造了一个新概念叫做 “价值创业” ，
也鼓励大家多多价值创业，价值投资

自从Crypto进入熊市，这一年折腾了很久，尝试过很多东西。

无论是做产品还是做内容都觉得比较难实现，要么是觉得天花板太低，要么是觉得很快会被大模型本身碾过去

今天回看AI行业，
- 做应用层的最终都凄惨的给大模型公司找场景，找不到的已经死掉了，找到的饭碗被大模型抢了；
- 做基建层的基本没有小登的机会，数据中心这些玩意实际上还是房地产，需要看看鱼头对谁，看看谁能和红血/蓝血家族离的够近
- 做倒爷的快速致富，但也依然焦虑于这个生意还能持续多久，壁垒能在那里。

尝试了很多之后才意识到价值投资的实际感受，好生意是相通的，能规模化、不太需要顶级CEO、客户愿意持续为产品支付溢价。

进而衍生到新的思考“像创业一样投资，像投资一样创业”

最终收敛为：
- 不去追宏大叙事（大概率赢不了）
- 多做小而美、利润率高、不累、标准化的业务，不断的赚现金流，然后不断的在便宜的价格中买入一样模式的公司
- 然后在路上慢慢想自己可以整出什么伟大的公司

感觉花了半年想通了这一点，之后多分享这方面的思考。
其实满足上面标准的一个很好的案例就是hyperliquid

text:
AI 玩「狼人杀」已经会主动卖队友了，甚至能借此把自己洗成全场最受信任的人。

Dwarkesh 最近花了约 2 万美元，做了个挺有意思的 Agent Benchmark，叫 Clocktower Bench。

让 10–12 个 AI 分成好人和邪恶阵营，互相私聊、交换线索、编造谎言、公开投票，最后用 386 场比赛评估不同模型的表现。

有一局 GPT-6 Astra 假扮调查员，主动指认自己的邪恶队友。队友被处决后，身份得到验证，其他玩家反而更信任它，最后成功获胜。

但看完文章，我更关注另一个发现。

在这个 Benchmark 中，OpenAI 较新模型的领先优势主要体现在识破骗局上。它们会不断对照前后的证据，重新判断谁更可疑，而部分 Claude 模型更容易过早相信某条线索。

这让我想到平时做 Agent Eval，面对错误信息或相互矛盾的工具结果，Agent 能不能及时发现问题、修正之前的判断，其实很值得单独测试。

作者还开源了完整的评测 Harness 和对局记录，可以自己复现、分析，甚至和 AI 直接对战。挺推荐做 Agent 研究的朋友看看。

text:
卧槽？？阿里巴巴淘宝App被扒出在用户本地偷偷装了个模型来监控用户购物行为？？？

有小红书网友排查手机存储时，称在淘宝私有目录的 NGUserIntent 文件夹里，发现了一套模型文件。
系统提示词直接写着：“你是一个淘宝购后场景电商推荐系统的导购专家，擅长挖掘用户意图。”

据这位网友描述，这是一个约 5 亿参数的 Qwen2模型。
从展示的配置看，它被设定使用设备的 GPU 进行本地推理。
相当于在你的手机里放了一位 AI 导购，用你的算力，琢磨你买完这一单，下一单还可能想买什么。

我查了一下，淘宝团队今年发表的 RecGPT-Mobile 论文，确实介绍过类似方案：把小模型部署到手机端，根据点击、收藏、加购、购买等行为，推测用户接下来可能搜索什么，再用于商品推荐。

举个例子，刚买完手机，接下来可能需要手机壳、贴膜或者充电器。
按照这种设计，判断这些潜在需求的计算，有一部分就在用户自己的手机上完成。
这也是一个挺具体的端侧 AI 应用：用户提供购物行为，手机提供算力，模型负责琢磨下一步该推荐什么商品。

我更在意的是，如果模型确实在用户不知情的情况下被下载、运行，为什么不能提前说清楚，让用户自己决定？

今天是一个导购模型。如果这样的功能可以在用户不知情的情况下加进来，以后还会有什么任务在手机上运行？
会分析哪些数据、占用多少资源，又由谁来决定？

安装一个购物 App，不应该等于接受它今后安排的所有本地计算。不能每次都等用户翻文件夹，才知道自己的手机又被安排了什么工作。

text:
RE: The claim that TSMC will enter memory and disrupt the big three memory makers

This doesn't make sense. As far as I know, TSMC has been working on this project for more than five years, but it would be a mistake to assume what they're building is commodity DRAM. TSMC has no DRAM IP, no DRAM patents, and none of the relevant technology.

I think the term "3D DRAM" is what's causing the misunderstanding.

After talking with industry experts, I believe this is the correct way to read the reports of TSMC entering DRAM.

TSMC's earlier published research gives a good sense of the direction.

At the 2025 VLSI Symposium, TSMC presented a memory technology based on oxide semiconductors, using a cell made of one transistor and one capacitor (1T1C). The goal was to integrate this memory into advanced logic chips and give processors a cache with low power and low latency.

The key feature of the design is that the memory array is built directly into the back end of line (BEOL) interconnect layers of the logic chip. Conventional DRAM is manufactured as a separate chip.

To build the memory array in the interconnect layers of an advanced logic chip, TSMC used select transistors with an oxide semiconductor channel and capacitors fabricated with a low temperature process.

According to TSMC, the test chip, which integrates memory and logic on a single die, operated at 0.75V. Data retention exceeded 128ms, random read/write cycle time was under 8ns, and endurance was above 10¹⁴ cycles. TSMC positioned the technology as a processor cache that offers higher density than SRAM while keeping power consumption and latency low.

So TSMC would be producing 3D DRAM as a next generation technology to replace SRAM. And not in large volumes, either.

Anyone saying TSMC will make DDR or LPDDR has no idea what they're talking about.

text:
美国 401(k) 投资加密货币的规则进入白宫最后审查

美国劳工部制定的一项退休计划投资规则已经在 11月5日 送交白宫审查。如果能生效就代表了 401(k) 退休计划将更容易把 Bitcoin、其他加密资产，以及私募股权、房地产等另类资产相关产品加入投资选项。

401(k) 是美国常见的雇主退休储蓄计划，类似于中国的养老金体系，劳工部今年 3 月提出一份草案希望可以在 401(k) 计划中弱化投资加密货币等审查流程，如果能成立则意味着可能会有大量的资金进入到 bitcoin:native 等主流（合规 ETF）加密货币领域。

截至到目前公布的数据中，401(k) 计划的资产规模约为 10.8 万亿美元。哪怕只有 1% 的资产能进入到加密资产领域，就是 1,080 亿美元。这将极大的缓解 Bitcoin 的流动性缺乏问题。

当然我个人感觉通过的问题应该不大，但是通过以后的配置可能还会纠结一段时间，如果真能有 1% 以上的配置，那 BTC 的牛市应该会再开启一波了。毕竟现在 BTC 的总市值才 1.52 万亿，1,080 亿就相当于 7% 的市值了。

5. Write down all your backup codes on paper, store it somewhere safe (fireproof and waterproof)
6. Bookmark every exchange and dApp websites. Never open them from Google or Telegram links

Telegram
9. Under Privacy, turn on Two-Step Verification (its a password), use Passkey and set Stars for Messages so random people cannot DM you
10. Check Active Sessions and delete anything you don't recognise
11. Set your phone number to Nobody
12. Never open files people send you, even from friends. Their account could be hacked
13. Ignore any "free to catch up" with Calendly links, you can catch up over Telegram message itself 
14. Disable Auto-Download Media (under Data and Storage)

Wallets
15. Seed phrase on paper or metal. Never in a notes app or cloud or Notion
16. Cold wallets for large funds, best to use a multisig with cold wallets (p.s best to offramp more into your bank so you can sleep at night)
17. Split wallets to mitigate single attack vector: small hot wallet for dApps, cold wallet for the rest
19. Revoke old unlimited approvals (https://t.co/gSUIwxMJTD)

Devices (Mac checklist https://t.co/qxB7ux7iKx by @0x_Osprey) 
20. FileVault + firewall on, auto login off
21. Auto updates on
22. Delete browser extensions you don't use
23. Separate browser (or device) just for crypto
24. Never run a recruiter's "coding challenge" especially if its something to install

Misc
25. Don't use Zoom or Microsoft teams if you have to take a call
26. Remember you are not a VIP, no journalist is going to want to interview you for your takes nor will companies send you emails / letters to warn you of a compromised account
27. Some of the contacts that you saved on Telegram could be compromised, saving as contact doesn't do anything 
28. Take note of some of the trading terminals that you have funds on, if the largest exchange can be compromised what more these smaller ones
29. Write a plan for if you get hacked, and leave one for your family
30. Remember to message @seal_911_bot if you have any emergencies @_SEAL_Org 

Stay paranoid.

text:
X AI ALGORITHM UPDATE 🚨

X updated their open source algorithm yesterday and the early likes matter even more now. Small accounts should focus on: writing posts people hit like on and read till the end (so write to be read)

tl;dr:

- X's open source code got new scores on Nov 5, the first change in 3 weeks
- likes: 0.66 → 0.708 (highest yet)
- time spent on a post: 0.006 → 0.0075
- tapping into a post: 0.3 → 0.274
- opening a video: 0.02 → 0
- new rule: AI replies may get flagged under big accounts as "llm slop" and may not reach the person's notifications 

lesson learned: a tap isn't the win anymore. Someone staying and liking is.

full details:

- The new numbers

Up: likes 0.66 → 0.708, time spent on a post 0.006 → 0.0075, shares 2 → 2.118.

Down: tapping into a post 0.3 → 0.274, staying 10+ seconds after a tap 0.4 → 0.385, opening a video 0.02 → 0.

"Not interested" got a bit harsher, -52.27 → -53.07.

Copy link, replies, quotes, DM shares and follows didn't move.

X didn't explain any of this. It's just what the code says now.

(I check the open source algo daily with Claude and share updates with you)

- Look at where this has gone in a month

In early October a like was worth 0.5. Now it's 0.708.

Time spent was 0.004. Now it's 0.0075, nearly double.

A tap was 0.3 and it's going down.

Every change points the same way. X keeps paying more for people who stay.

- Why that matters if you're small

My read: you can't win on big numbers, but you can win on the people who do see your post. If they stay and like it, that counts for more today than it did last week. And those early likes also decide which new post gets the extra push.

- Video and your profile

X also switched on two new guesses in its ranking: how long someone keeps watching after they open a video, and how long they spend on a profile after tapping it.

I can't tell you what those are worth. The only file that lists them is out of date, so I won't guess a number.

My read: opening a video dropped to 0 the same day because X cares more about people who keep watching. So make the first seconds count, and make your profile worth sticking around on.

- A new rule for replies under big accounts

X runs an AI check on replies under accounts with over 250K followers. Flagged replies can get a label that lasts 14 to 30 days. One of the flags is literally called "llm slop" (AI slop, as I read it).

That part isn't new. This is: X's rules now say a labeled reply or mention doesn't reach the person's notifications unless they follow you.

Grey badge accounts and accounts X rates as highly credible skip this label. Small accounts get no such pass.

I can see the rule, I can't see if every notification goes through it yet. Either way, write your own replies.

- What didn't change

Your new posts still get their extra push in the first 2 hours and first 200 views, and they still don't get cut first.

Here's a recap of what you should be doing:

- likes just hit 0.708, the most they've ever been worth
- each second someone spends on your post is worth 25% more than last week
- staying 10+ seconds after a tap earns 0.385 on top of the tap
- reply in your own words, under big accounts especially
- make your profile worth a visit, X now guesses how long people spend there
- for video, hold attention early, just getting the open now scores 0
- being read to the end also helps X find you new readers
- originals from accounts below 50K can jump to around spot 16
- early viewers liking it is what wins that lift
- your first 2 hours and 200 views are the window, so publish when your people are online
- the biggest single number is still 20, for someone copying your link
- quotes, DM shares and replies earn 5 apiece
- back and forth between mutuals is worth 20, so follow back your regulars
- strangers only get shown your originals
- the 1st like and the 32nd like each open another route to new people
- a second post of yours in the same feed drops to 62%, so make one count
- the video lists want clips over 10 seconds
- +4 when a post is likely to earn you a new follower
- your pinned post can affect the whole account, so take a look at it

What you should NOT be doing:

- pasting AI replies under big accounts, "llm slop" is a real flag at X
- copy-paste replies, a duplicate label means they never get notified
- chasing the tap, it's down to 0.274 and falling
- off-topic posts, one likely "not interested" costs -53.07
- a video that only gets opened earns nothing for the open
- publishing at 3am burns your 2 hour window
- relying on replies and reposts to reach new people, they stay with your followers
- getting an insult label, non-followers won't see that post at all
- low quality and misinfo labels bring a warning, and non-followers can't like or share
- adult media in 3 of your last 5 posts gets the whole account labeled
- X rechecks videos for hidden content at 64 and 512 likes
- piling your replies under a big account's post can sink your own score
- one label on the account and non-followers stop seeing you
- a link to a badly rated site in your pinned post risks a 7 day label
- reusing your own wording word for word risks the copypasta flag
- pairing a low quality link with tags of strangers looks like spam to X
- engagement bait gets labeled no matter how big you are
- posting several in a row, they fight each other for the same feed
- hashtag stuffing does nothing
- counting on bookmarks, they're worth 0
- expecting For You to show a post past 48 hours

Let's play it out. Let's pause American AI. Let's ban RSI. Put a moratorium on all the data centers. America's progress will severely slow down. China's will inevitably keep going. They don't care about your American moratorium. They will continue to build RSI anyway, (this is guaranteed) and they will most likely keep open-sourcing models like they already do.

So the job loss happens anyway. I have my own small business, and I also work for a major company. The side teams are going to use it like they already do, I'm going to use it, and people in other small businesses are going to use it to replace editors, gig workers, programmers, and software engineers who might have done small projects here and there.

Even with the YouTube teams I work with, they already plan on replacing all of their editors in one years time. - they will just simply switch to Chinese models.

The job loss is going to happen regardless: the editing, the assistants, customer service, and a huge chunk of gig work will all be done by free open-source models from China. And unless you're banning self-driving cars too, the majority of rideshare will eventually go with it.

Except now, the upside is no longer in America. The labs, the chips, and the tax revenue are all going to go to China. If you think advanced AI is dangerous, you still have to explain how an American pause protects us from systems developed abroad and whether it leaves us less able to defend ourselves. text:
Utah sent an undercover agent to place about $115 in sports bets on Kalshi. Now the two people who started Kalshi are charged with 13 felonies, and the top charge alone carries up to 15 years in prison.

The day after the charges came down, investors gave Kalshi $1 billion.

Here's how the sting worked. In September, a special agent with the Utah attorney general's office opened a Kalshi account with a Utah address, a Utah phone number and a Utah debit card. Before his first bet, $10 on the Cowboys against the Giants, the app asked him to confirm his location. He told it he was in Utah, and it took his money. He did that 12 times over 11 days, on games like Utah vs. Utah State and a Real Salt Lake match.

Kalshi's cut on each bet was somewhere between 3 and 78 cents. So the company made less than $10 off the bets Utah is now using to go after its CEO and COO personally. And that top charge comes from Utah's racketeering law, the same kind of statute prosecutors use on organized crime.

The obvious question is why Kalshi didn't just shut off Utah. It clearly knows how. It already blocks Nevada and Washington because a settlement and a court order made it. DraftKings pulled its sports and politics markets out of Utah the same night the charges were filed, FanDuel did it the next day, and Fanatics shut down everything there on November 4.

Kalshi stayed because of how the company is built. DraftKings runs on licenses from gambling regulators in more than 20 states, so when one state comes after you with criminal charges, you get out fast and protect the rest. Kalshi has exactly one license, from a federal agency called the CFTC. Its whole $40 billion valuation depends on the idea that this one federal license overrides state gambling laws, and quietly walking away from Utah would cut against that argument everywhere else.

The federal government is backing Kalshi on this, and pretty aggressively. The CFTC and the Justice Department sued Utah two days before the charges. Their complaint says that if Kalshi turned away Utah residents, it would be breaking a federal "impartial access" rule that requires exchanges to serve everyone.

So the founders are stuck. Utah wants them to stop taking bets from Utahns or face prison, and the federal government is in court saying they aren't allowed to stop.

This goes way past Utah, too. The CFTC has sued 10 states since April. On the other side, 37 states signed a brief backing Utah in its appeal.

Sequoia and Wellington, who co-led the $1 billion round, are betting on one legal question, whether federal commodities law beats state gambling law. If the courts say yes, Utah's criminal case could fall apart along with every state lawsuit against Kalshi. A federal judge in Utah already said no back in August. The 10th Circuit is up next, and this looks like it's headed to the Supreme Court.

Kind of fitting for a company that lets you bet on almost anything that its biggest investors now have $1 billion riding on how a court case turns out.

text:
“Almost all of my founder friends agree that the only reliable sources of funding for risky early ideas are rich people who angel invest as a hobby and accelerators like YC.”

This is a reality of the growth of multistage platforms, which are structurally and empirically consensus oriented.

Venture capital has reached a point that will be familiar to economists:

1) a mixed market 
2) a bubble occurs
3) capital inflows expand
4) the bubble bursts 
5) rapid consolidation
6) incumbents capture core markets 
7) the periphery is vacated 
8) the rise of specialists 

This is an accelerated version of “resource partitioning”, as described by Carroll & Swaminathan — with their original case study looking at the beer industry:

Market consolidation up to the 1980s (a result of economies of scale, M&A, marketing costs) led to consumers growing bored of dominant “industrial beer”.

Then came the craft beer revolution of specialist microbreweries, taking the peripheral market of unique beer styles for the beer enthusiast customer base.

So, microbreweries grew from effectively 0% of retail dollars in 1980 to about 25% of retail dollars today. 

On top of this, industrial brewers now use microbreweries as external labs who experiment with concepts in the market which the industrial brewer could take to scale. 

So, in VC terms, we are in 1980 — with the early surge of small specialists being felt in programmes like @govclab, or funds like @briansin’s GPx.

<$10M funds are around 1% of VC allocation today. I expect that to grow to >10% over the next few years as it becomes clearer that the discovery layer needs funding if the venture strategy is to maintain an edge.

More: https://t.co/0Ei2dryR3J

三年前我认为：

1. 应用公司都会有自己的模型，不是 base model，是 workflow 中间用于判断/检索的模型

2. 模型训练本质是流水线工程，最重要的是数据质量

3. 前端和后端开发会逐渐死掉，模型微调应该是后端掌握的基础能力

4. 不存在【垂直模型】这个赛道，模型 + 行业知识做搜索或者其他工作流即可碾压所谓的【垂直模型】

这些判断有对有错，但勇于下判断让我看到了行业的前沿，进而借助看到的机会：【给模型公司供给训练数据】，赚到了合成数据的钱

但我始终认为数据本质还是生意模式，没想到会成为今年这样火爆的赛道，没什么可惜的，只是认知不够

——————

如今我有了一些新判断：

0. 到2030年前，大方向是抛弃叙事、价值回归，就像来到了熊市一样

1. 视频领域不管什么方向，技术和模型上做不出差异化，只会有阶段性领先，都要回归到做生态来加强用户粘性

2. 端侧 AI 是伪命题，就像三年前他们在讨论用线性 RNN 逆袭 Transformer 一样

3. 但是 desktop 的本地模型应用是真命题，可以结合本地使用数据做训练和调整，形成粘性，在最近一些素材库管理工具、输入法上已有体现

4. Pexels、Pixabay 这样的素材和版权网站会逐渐死掉，搜索标签不应该是对人的

5. 理解只是生成的一部分。理解最好的场景是给生成打标，所以它天然和终端用户走的很远，成交的客户只会是中间态的大B，而理解模型做不出差异化，所以这里的大B如果需求真的大会倾向于自建

虽然从 research 上讲，大家一直认为理解和生成是两个大的分类，但无法对应到商业上。二者是一体两面的，理解为生成服务，生成展现终端价值（所以可能 UMM 在商业上是对的

6. 进而，理解模型没有单独的创业机会，不管是文本类还是视频类。文本类的显著代表是 Jev，但类 Jev 的公司最终不会有超过两家，Jev 本身更多是因为 OpenAI Co-Founder 的 title

7. 综上，视频理解非常不适合 startup，多模态理解和视频理解是一回事（虽然我真的很喜欢多模态，但那只是我喜欢自己的青春

author: jukan05
quoted_text:
I'd like to believe LTAs are durable too. But take one example.

Analog chipmaker onsemi said this in 2023.
On January 5, 2023, at JPMorgan's CES forum, CEO Hassane El-Khoury was asked how much LTSAs would still hold once the shortage eased. His answer: “They are a legally binding agreement ’cause they’re a liability for the customer because they’re take or pay.” He also said he would not accept a customer reopening price talks just because it could get the same parts 10% cheaper elsewhere.

On October 30, 2023, on the Q3 earnings call, onsemi cut its SiC shipment forecast for the year from $1 billion to more than $800 million after one automotive OEM reduced demand. An analyst asked how this could happen when the company had been saying its LTSAs were legally binding. The same CEO reaffirmed that they were binding, but said he did not want to enforce the contracts just to push inventory onto a customer whose demand had dropped. If it worked for both sides, terms could be adjusted customer by customer, whether by a quarter, a year, or longer.

In its 10-K filings, onsemi also states that it amended LTSAs with some strategic customers by mutual agreement in 2024, and changed delivery schedules and committed volumes on some LTSAs in 2025 as demand shifted.

Microchip is another case. Customers in its Preferred Supply Program (PSP) originally had to place 12 months of orders and could not cancel or reschedule them unless Microchip raised prices. On its November 2025 earnings call, however, the CEO said the company had accepted some cancellations and pushouts so customers could adjust their backlog. On the same call, the CFO separately addressed the multiyear LTSAs the company had signed. Some of those contracts were still in effect, he said, but customers had been allowed to defer taking delivery of committed volumes by one to two years if they needed to.

Every time I see cases like these, I doubt how much memory makers' LTAs will protect earnings in a downcycle. Right now the most reliable thing is the prepayments and deposits themselves. That cash can go into capacity expansion today.

I can picture hyperscalers with no DRAM inventory continuing to buy at current prices. But once inventory has piled up, will they keep taking every committed unit at the same price? I have a hard time picturing memory makers holding customers to the high contract price all the way through.

The LTA itself may never be broken and may stay in place. But if both sides agree to push this year's volumes into next year or two years out, this year's earnings estimates come down. If price gets renegotiated too, margin estimates have to come down as well.

Again, I agree LTAs are sturdier than they used to be. What I question is whether, after demand turns, memory makers can still earn 80% margins on contracts signed during the upturn and keep collecting hundreds of billions of dollars in profit because of those LTAs.

X updated its algorithm again on November 5

If you are struggling with engagement read this:

- Likes are more important than ever
- Their score increased from 0.66 to 0.708
- Time spent reading your post is up 25%
- Getting people to open your post is less important 
- Videos are still important but getting someone to open one is worth 0
- the most important thing is how long people actually watch
- The first 2 hours and 200 views are crucial
- Early likes help your posts reach new people

(Small accounts can benefit a lot from this)

X is now detecting AI-generated replies under accounts with over 250K followers

These replies might not even reach their notifications

Copy-paste replies are also getting punished

Posting several times in a row can hurt your reach

So in fact the algorithm is clearly prioritizing people who actually spend time consuming your content

My advice is simple, stop chasing impressions and focus on making posts people actually want to read

I am not an expert but these are the latest changes I have been following

text:
今日妖币分析： $ONE +  $AIN

$ONE：24小时暴涨54%，距离前高仅差4.8%，这是要继续冲高，还是最后一波诱多？

$AIN：币安 Alpha 单日暴涨33%后又从高点跌近四成，这场游戏到底是谁在收割谁？

1. ONE：老公链的最后一搏，还是空头猎杀？

24小时涨幅54.52%，成交量接近2963万美元。
未平仓合约约188万美元，预测资金费率-0.083%/4小时。
价格距离24小时高点仅差4.8%，换手非常激烈。

这里有个值得关注的信号：价格大幅上涨，但资金费率却转负，说明永续合约市场空头支付资金费率，多空博弈明显。

如果价格继续走强，空头可能被进一步挤压，形成逼空行情；但如果冲高后放量滞涨，也要警惕高位多空双杀。

我的判断： 目前更像是高波动博弈，重点观察前高附近能否放量突破。突破站稳才有继续上涨的基础，否则不排除冲高回落。

2. AIN：一天振幅2.5倍，Alpha 小盘币又开始猎杀了？

单日涨幅33.16%，最高触及0.2346。
当前价格0.1441，较高点回撤约38.6%。
单日成交约98.4万美元，流动性约88万美元。
持币地址约1.9万个。

AIN 最大的问题不是涨幅，而是流动性。

text:
a few words about my thinking around amplifying clanker builders and tokens from this account. 

first of all: builders need distribution more than anything else. 

I know, because I’ve been one myself, and I’ve spent years in the onchain trenches with builders and traders alike.

it’s one of the easiest things to give, and it’s functionally free…. yet most ecosystems and ecosystem leads fail to do it properly. 

and that’s probably because they’re scared.

they’re scared to accidentally promote a rug, or a soft rug, or an outright scam. which, fair enough. it’s a minefield out there, and in the golden age of AI slop, some of the mines are difficult to sweep. 

but I’m not scared.

I’ll do my best to vet new projects before amplifying them here. I’ve already been actively reaching out to builders to open comms and make sure they can get the support they need to build for the long term, and will continue to do so. 

I’ll share clanker eco projects that I think are promising because those builders deserve the initial attention, and the opportunity to earn more of it over time (scarce asset that it is). And I’ll share memes with good teams because memes are entertaining and it would be super boring around here without them. 

I’ll continue to buy some of these tokens on my public fomo as a signal of support too, and I won’t sell them.

But despite all that, some of these won’t work out, and that’s ok. 

we’re all adults here and we understand the game we’re playing: the speculative attention game. 

but speculative attention games that can allow real builders to bootstrap real projects they otherwise could not build, so that’s pretty based. 

I think there’s a whole hierarchy of “free” distribution that can eventually be earned in this eco, including follows and shares from the @clanker_world account, other @base leaders, etc. I’ll also work on a plan for how these kinds of “vouches” can be earned over time.

but as for me and this account, my top priority is to lift up clanker builders, old and new. I’ll do my best to curate them carefully and give them a chance to earn your longer term support (or not).

imo, this is the only way we can win together.

text:
AI is making knowledge, creativity and reasoning increasingly accessible to everyone.

For most of us who have spent years sharpening our minds, this raises some unsettling questions.

What happens to careers, identity and sense of purpose when AI can already do much of what we do, often better?

“Learn AI” is superficial and inadequate answer when it involves wholesome wellbeing of the generation that follows and we have a responsibility to be the bridge.

Much of the self-worth has been a projection from being knowledgeable, capable, respected and needed for clarity. What happens when these qualities no longer set humans apart?

Perhaps this is an opportunity to rethink what we work towards: greater financial independence, deeper relationships, stronger communities, causes worth pursuing and the freedom to explore ideas simply for the joy of understanding.

AI may free us to accomplish things we never imagined possible.

The harder part may be learning to value ourselves without constantly measuring what we can do better than others.

A deeply unsettling thought, perhaps also a liberating one. #AIThoughts #Mentorship 
#Relationships #Swadharma

text:
Even though I disagree with some of the assumptions made, this is a good write-up of the discussion, and I appreciate the perspective on the benefits and the conclusion that Glamsterdam should proceed.

There really are two classes of “invariants”
- *Parameters*, eg, gas cost of an operation or block time
- Pricing *mechanisms* for operations

Contracts should not rely on the first class not changing. However mechanisms should be updated ideally in a non-breaking manner.

Glamsterdam has a mix of both changes. Unfortunately, a planned mechanism update (EIP-8037) produces breaking changes where we should not expect some to be, hence the additional delay

In any case, if either of the two categories sees some change, every effort should be made to identify and support apps that are directly or indirectly affected. It could be that the gas cost update makes a specific use case relatively more expensive, or cheaper, changing app economics.

A repository was released for app devs to identify the changes https://t.co/H3XuZZZZVL Internal and external audits have already led to active outreach, this step is designed for last mile coverage

text:
看了九神和老夫子今天的分享，结合最近 UAI 的走势，有了一些新的交易感悟。

近期二级山寨市场出现了一些变化，恶庄越来越多，针对散户的收割手段也越来越极端：快速插针、深 V 反转、反复诱多诱空。

接下来，高倍币的反弹机会依然值得参与，但必须减少出手次数，尤其是追高时，更要警惕数据背后的真实性和意图。

以 UAI 为例。

空投前，市场就已经出现了大量空单，从 0.3 一路砸到 0.07。空投前两天，价格又被拉到高位，随后开始发放空投。

这个时间点和价格位置都很微妙。我不太相信庄家会突然大发善心，专门给所有人送钱。

空投开始抛售时，盘面再次出现集中砸盘，但价格很快被拉回，甚至不断创新高。几次链上都出现了疑似抛售的信号，却没有真正走出预期中的崩盘行情。

现在回头看，这不排除是一场诱导市场参与者误判的局。让盯着链上数据的人以为抛压已经出现，进而做出错误的交易决策。

第一次遇到这种情况时，我直觉上就不认为它会直接崩盘，所以没有贸然做空。后面虽然又看到了几次类似信号，但也没有继续参与。

1. 链上数据是证据，不是答案，数据优势也可能成为认知上的陷阱。

2. 看任何一个动作，都要多想一步：庄家为什么选择在这个时间、这个位置这样做？这件事对他有什么好处？如果看起来不符合利益逻辑，就更应该警惕背后的目的。

3. 少赚好过多亏。看不懂就不做，错过机会也没什么。市场永远不缺机会。

最后，还是回到最初的交易原则：

静下心做自己擅长的事情，减少无效交易，保持清醒的能力，独立思考。

quoted_text:
MEXC到底干了什么？美国财政部为什么直接对它下狠手？

美国认为MEXC已经成了受制裁实体、洗钱网络和网络犯罪分子的资金中转站，而且平台自己的反洗钱机制根本没能有效拦住这些资金。

FinCEN披露，2021年5月至2026年5月，至少167亿美元涉嫌非法资金经MEXC流转。具体涉及四类问题：

俄罗斯制裁规避：近15亿美元资金与俄罗斯制裁规避有关，其中2.32亿美元涉及美、欧、英直接制裁的实体。最严重的是，MEXC在Garantex被美国制裁四年多以后，仍持续与其及继任者Grinex交易，直到2026年6月。

伊朗资金网络：约18.7亿美元资金与伊朗相关，其中超过10亿美元涉及MEXC与40多家伊朗加密交易所的直接往来；约2200万美元涉及伊朗央行、伊斯兰革命卫队及其圣城旅。

朝鲜制裁规避：MEXC曾帮助美国制裁的朝鲜洗钱人员Sim Hyon Sop接收约35万美元，即使对方早已被列入制裁名单。

网络犯罪：约19.9亿美元涉及网络犯罪行为人，包括诈骗、勒索软件和暗网交易。仅2022年至2024年，MEXC就收到超过3790万美元疑似勒索软件付款。

美国这次真正动用的手段，是禁止美国金融机构处理任何涉及MEXC的资金转移，包括加密货币转账。

text:
Highlights and key takeaways from DeSci Summit Mumbai this week 👇

→ The IP question decides whether a biologist can use frontier models at all. Several PhD labs bar ChatGPT and Claude outright, since prompting them leaks unpublished research.

→ Ask a frontier model to design a 10 amino acid peptide that binds and inhibits the SARS-CoV main protease and the request gets flagged. Both refusals ran live on stage, and the same prompt at @biosdiscovery returned an answer plus a route into a binder generation pipeline.

→ Finding a binder is finding a needle in a haystack. Doing it in silico only became possible after @GoogleDeepMind in 2020 and RFdiffusion from the Baker Lab.

→ Ten scored binders come back within ten minutes. The models sit on 200 GPUs, which opens the platform to anyone who shows up today.

→ RFdiffusion 4 runs on Mac, ported by @GeeveGeorge and currently the fastest RFdiffusion MLX model. A scientist designing a drug keeps every piece of data on their own machine.

→ A Qwen 8B model runs at 100 tokens/sec on M1 through M5 using custom kernels, ahead of ZSpec and Splash. The team calls it spec metal.

→ Qwen orchestrates and RFdiffusion designs, so drug discovery runs fully locally. The @biosdiscovery CLI is agent-native, built on the view that agents will be the ones using this software.

→ In coding and math the verifier is fast. In biology the verifier is the world, which is why wet lab demand rises as more people design medicines with AI.

→ Robios ran its first live demonstration. It loads and unloads the machine and records conditions like temperature, so two runs can be compared.

→ Human in the loop throughout. A senior scientist watches from home, gives feedback at any time, and steers it mid-run.

→ Competitors buy their robots from OEMs at prices most labs are unable to afford. Robios is built on open source and aimed at NCBS Bangalore and a wet lab in Mumbai.

→ Local agentic swarms are next, 10 to 20 agents on a MacBook reading real research papers and citing them. Citation is how hallucination gets reduced.

→ A research proposal takes around 116 hours to write. Grant acceptance has declined to 19% in the UK, 13% for US health research, and 8% for EU early career awards.

→ Publication costs roughly $12,000 at Nature and 17 months. @openlabsbio puts those first steps in one place, with an index covering failed and ongoing work, challenges for calling in skills, vaults funding first studies, and a launchpad for pre-company raises.

Idea, lab, funded IP, product.

Every layer we build shortens one of those and opens the next.

Full talks ↓

text:
four days in, and the conversations got bigger than the conference itself. 🇮🇳

a little late, but @EFDevcon final day in mumbai deserved a proper recap.

from @ETHGlobal Pragma to technical discussions and conversations with brilliant leaders and creative minds, here’s what stood out.

> ETHGlobal Pragma Mumbai

a different conference experience. one track, curated talks and focused conversations. less running between stages, more time understanding what people are building and why.

> the open source network state

Balaji S. Srinivasan’s talk at @ETHIndiaco explored a bigger question: what happens when communities can build institutions and coordinate globally through open technology? this conversation goes far beyond crypto.

> privacy beyond the buzzword

HOPR’s private transport, peer payments and Gnosis VPN workshop raised an important question: how do we communicate without exposing unnecessary metadata?

> the infrastructure underneath decentralisation

privacy isn’t just about transactions. protecting network communication, reducing metadata leakage and resisting censorship are fundamental to keeping permissionless systems open.

> the people shaping the ecosystem

met incredible leaders, builders and creative minds. some of the best conversations happened away from the stage, without slides or agendas.

> beyond the protocol

AI, finance, identity, privacy and open infrastructure are becoming increasingly connected. the boundaries are blurring, and that’s where some interesting opportunities are emerging.

> the creative layer

this industry needs more people thinking deeply about product experience, brand, storytelling and culture. technology moves quickly, but communicating its value matters just as much.

> a little perspective

don’t let conference criticism, hot takes and noise distract you from your own work. focus on building, learning and contributing. some people might need a little Burnol to get over their conference experience. 😂

> and the merch hunters?

they’re everywhere. don’t confuse a few people chasing free merch with the actual builders and potential of an entire ecosystem.

one thought to close the week:

be kind. give people credit. share knowledge, make introductions and celebrate good work.

culture isn’t built through conference stages or social media commentary. it’s built through how we treat people and contribute to the ecosystem.

ethereum’s biggest opportunity isn’t just what its technology can do today. it’s what it enables people to build, own, coordinate and organise tomorrow.

that’s the bigger story.

i explore these intersections through The Protocol, my research and writing project on crypto, product, design, culture and the future of the internet.

designprotocol (dot) substack (dot) com

and a special thank you to the organisers, volunteers, support staff and the entire Ethereum team. so much work happens behind the scenes. genuinely appreciate everyone who made this experience possible. ❤️

bringing @EFDevcon to India was one of the best decisions. the energy, hospitality and people made this a wonderful experience.

mumbai, you delivered. 🇮🇳
